classification.difficultyReason: The student rewrites the phase-shifted cosine as a negated cosine, equates the two models, solves for cos, and takes the first positive inverse-cosine time. This is a few linked steps with a small insight about the phase shift, and no graph is supplied. It is slightly above direct evaluation and below p13-q10.

content.prompt: Find the first time after $t=0$ that the two heights are equal. Give your answers correct to 2 decimal places.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The depths, in metres, of water at two wharves are modelled by $d_P(t)=2\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)+5$ and $d_Q(t)=3\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi(t-6)}{6}\right)+4.4$, where $t$ is the time in hours after midday.

answer.worked:
Since $\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}-\pi\right)=-\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right)$,
$$\begin{align*}d_Q(t)&=-3\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right)+4.4\end{align*}$$
Equate the depths.
$$\begin{align*}2\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right)+5&=-3\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right)+4.4\\5\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right)&=-0.6\\\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right)&=-0.12\\t&=\frac{6}{\pi}\cos^{-1}(-0.12)\\t&\approx3.23\end{align*}$$
The principal value gives the first time after $t=0$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The heights, in metres, of a cabin on each of two Ferris wheels are modelled by $h_A(t)=-20\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{30}\right)+21$ and $h_B(t)=-10\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi(t-30)}{30}\right)+17$, where $t$ is the time in seconds.

answer.worked:
Since $\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{30}-\pi\right)=-\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{30}\right)$,
$$\begin{align*}h_B(t)&=10\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{30}\right)+17\end{align*}$$
Equate the heights.
$$\begin{align*}-20\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{30}\right)+21&=10\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{30}\right)+17\\30\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{30}\right)&=4\\\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{30}\right)&=\frac{2}{15}\\t&=\frac{30}{\pi}\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{15}\right)\\t&\approx13.72\end{align*}$$
The principal value gives the first time after $t=0$.
